descriptor: Early-warning intelligence system for rural and Critical Access Hospital management companies.

requirements.statement: The system must import public CMS HCRIS Medicare cost report files for rural and Critical Access Hospitals in Oklahoma and Texas.
The system must compute operating margin, days cash on hand, and days in A/R per hospital per year from the imported data.
The system must provide a free public Health Snapshot showing three years of trends for each hospital.
The system must flag hospitals with operating margin below 0%, days cash on hand below 30, or days in A/R rising two years in a row.
The system must store the exact values that triggered each flag.
The system must reject any AI-generated briefing containing a number not in the input data.
The system must allow operators to upload monthly exports per hospital, including general ledger, A/R aging, denials summary, and staffing.
The system must enforce database row-level security so each management company only sees its own hospitals.
The system must reject any file containing patient names, birth dates, or record numbers before it is stored or logged.
The system must detect duplicate uploads by file hash.
The system must convert exports from different hospital systems into a standard set of monthly metrics.
The system must mark unknown formats as 'needs mapping' rather than guessing.
The system must link every computed metric back to the file and row it came from.
The system must send a weekly email briefing every Monday at 6:00 AM Central.
The system must ensure every import, upload, normalization, and email is idempotent.
The system must surface a slipping hospital at least 4 weeks earlier than the operator's current reporting cycle.
The system must use Supabase for auth, Postgres, and storage.
The system must use Vercel for hosting and the Anthropic Claude API for AI.
The system must use Resend for email delivery.
The system must use Python for data work and Next.js for the web app.

releases.goal: Enable operator uploads with security and data normalization.

stories.title: Import CMS HCRIS Data
stories.narrative: As a system admin, I want to import CMS HCRIS data, so that I can compute financial metrics for hospitals.
acceptance: Given CMS HCRIS data is available, When the import process runs, Then the data is imported and metrics are computed.
Given invalid data format, When the import process runs, Then the data is rejected with an error message.
Trust: Every imported data point is traceable to its source file and row.
stories.task_guidance: Implement data import using Python scripts to read CMS HCRIS files and store results in Supabase Postgres.

stories.title: Compute Financial Metrics and Ensure Trust Spine
stories.narrative: As a system operator, I want to compute financial metrics from imported data, so that I can ensure accurate and trustworthy reporting.
acceptance: Given a set of imported data, when the system computes financial metrics, then it should produce a standard set of monthly metrics.
Given a computed metric, when traced, then it should link back to the original file and row it came from.
Trust: Given any computation, when logged, then it should include an audit trail linking metrics to source data.
stories.task_guidance: Implement computation logic to process imported data and generate metrics. Ensure each metric is linked to its source file and row in the audit trail.

stories.title: Public Health Snapshot Access
stories.narrative: As a public user, I want to access health snapshots, so that I can view hospital trends over three years.
acceptance: Given a hospital name, When searched, Then the system displays three years of trends.
Given a non-existent hospital, When searched, Then the system returns a 'not found' message.
Trust: Each trend figure shows the data year and notes public data lag.
stories.task_guidance: Develop a Next.js frontend to display health snapshots with data from Supabase.

stories.title: Implement Early Warning Flags
stories.narrative: As a system admin, I want to implement early warning flags, so that I can identify hospitals needing attention.
acceptance: Given computed metrics, When flagging criteria are met, Then the system flags the hospital.
Given missing data, When flagging criteria are checked, Then the system marks the hospital as 'not assessable'.
Trust: Each flag stores the exact values that triggered it.
stories.task_guidance: Implement flagging logic in Python to evaluate metrics and store results in Supabase.

stories.title: Operator Upload Functionality
stories.narrative: As an operator, I want to upload monthly exports, so that I can provide updated financial data for my hospitals.
acceptance: Given a valid export file, When uploaded, Then the system accepts and processes the file.
Given a duplicate file, When uploaded, Then the system rejects it with a duplicate message.
Trust: Each upload is checked for duplicates by file hash.
stories.task_guidance: Develop upload functionality using Next.js and Supabase storage, ensuring file hash checks for duplicates.

stories.title: Enforce Row-Level Security
stories.narrative: As a system admin, I want to enforce row-level security, so that each company only sees its own hospitals.
acceptance: Given a company user, When accessing data, Then only their hospitals are visible.
Given an unauthorized access attempt, When accessing data, Then access is denied.
Trust: Row-level security is enforced on all data queries.
stories.task_guidance: Configure Supabase row-level security policies to restrict data access by company ID.

stories.title: Generate AI Briefings
stories.narrative: As a system admin, I want to generate AI briefings, so that I can provide a summary of hospitals at risk.
acceptance: Given engine output, When generating a briefing, Then the briefing is created from valid data only.
Given invalid data in engine output, When generating a briefing, Then the briefing is rejected.
Trust: Each briefing is checked for grounding against the input data.
stories.task_guidance: Use the Anthropic Claude API to generate briefings and implement grounding checks before saving.

stories.title: Send Weekly Email Briefings
stories.narrative: As an operator, I want to receive weekly email briefings, so that I can stay informed about hospital statuses.
acceptance: Given a briefing is ready, When the email job runs, Then the briefing is emailed at 6:00 AM Central.
Given an email delivery failure, When the email job runs, Then a retry is attempted.
Trust: Each email sent is logged with a timestamp and recipient.
stories.task_guidance: Configure Resend for email delivery and schedule weekly email jobs using Vercel.

stories.title: Ensure Idempotency Across Processes
stories.narrative: As a system admin, I want to ensure idempotency across all processes, so that repeated runs do not alter outcomes.
acceptance: Given a process runs twice, When executed, Then the outcome remains unchanged.
Given a process interruption, When resumed, Then the process completes without duplication.
Trust: Each process logs its execution state to prevent duplication.
stories.task_guidance: Implement idempotency checks and logging for all processes using Python and Supabase.

stories.title: Reject Files with Sensitive Patient Information
stories.narrative: As a system operator, I want the system to reject files containing sensitive patient information, so that I can ensure compliance with data protection regulations.
acceptance: Given a file containing patient names, when uploaded, then the system should reject it before storage.
Given a file containing birth dates, when uploaded, then the system should reject it before logging.
Trust: Given a rejected file, when logged, then it should include an audit entry stating the reason for rejection.
failure_paths: Audit entry missing for rejected file
stories.task_guidance: Implement file validation logic to detect and reject files with patient names, birth dates, or record numbers before storage or logging.

stories.title: Convert Hospital System Exports to Standard Metrics
stories.narrative: As a system operator, I want to convert exports from different hospital systems into standard metrics, so that I can maintain consistency across reports.
acceptance: Given an export from a hospital system, when processed, then it should convert into a standard set of monthly metrics.
Given an export with an unknown format, when processed, then it should be marked as 'needs mapping'.
Trust: Given a conversion, when logged, then it should include an audit entry linking the export to the resulting metrics.
stories.task_guidance: Develop conversion logic to handle different hospital system exports and produce standard metrics. Implement a mechanism to flag unknown formats.

stories.title: Surface Slipping Hospitals Early
stories.narrative: As a system operator, I want to surface slipping hospitals at least 4 weeks earlier than the current reporting cycle, so that I can take timely action.
acceptance: Given hospital performance data, when analyzed, then slipping hospitals should be surfaced at least 4 weeks earlier than the current cycle.
Given a hospital flagged as slipping, when reviewed, then it should provide details on performance decline.
Trust: Given a slipping hospital alert, when logged, then it should include an audit entry with the analysis date and details.
failure_paths: Audit entry missing for slipping alert
stories.task_guidance: Implement analysis logic to detect and flag slipping hospitals based on performance data, ensuring early detection and logging.

stories.title: Handle Unknown Format Files
stories.narrative: As a data operator, I want the system to mark unknown formats as 'needs mapping', so that no incorrect assumptions are made about data structure.
acceptance: Given an uploaded file with an unknown format, When the system processes the file, Then the file is marked as 'needs mapping'.
Given an uploaded file with a known format, When the system processes the file, Then the file is processed normally without marking.
Trust: Given any file processing, Then the system logs the format status and decision in the audit trail.
failure_paths: File format is not recognized and is incorrectly processed.
File format is recognized but incorrectly marked as 'needs mapping'.
Audit trail fails to log the format status.
System crashes when encountering an unknown format.
Operator is not notified of the 'needs mapping' status.
stories.task_guidance: Implement a check during file upload that verifies the format against known formats. If unknown, flag the file and log the event in the audit trail.

agents.name: Briefing Agent
agents.purpose: Turns a company's currently-flagged hospitals (early_warning_flags, scoped through company_hospitals) into a grounded, human-readable weekly briefing. Every number Claude states must already exist in the engine's own output, or the briefing is rejected before it is ever saved.
agents.trigger: Weekly, Monday 6:00 AM Central, via the GitHub Actions cron in .github/workflows/weekly-briefing-email.yml (pipeline/weekly_briefing_email.py calls pipeline/briefing_agent.py once per company); can also be run on demand with --force.
inputs: early_warning_flags.criteria for the hospitals one company manages (joined through company_hospitals)
The exact numeric facts flattened from those criteria (briefing_agent.build_facts())
outputs: One briefings row per company per day (Postgres)
One weekly email per operator, sent via Resend, logged in weekly_briefing_emails
approval_gates: validate_flagged_hospital(): malformed or empty engine output is rejected before Claude is ever called (InvalidEngineOutput)

check_coverage() / grounding check: any hospital not named, or any number not present in the engine's own facts, rejects the whole briefing before it is saved (UngroundedBriefing / IncompleteBriefing)
escalation_rules: A rejected or failed briefing for one company is skipped and logged; it never blocks or corrupts another company's briefing in the same run
Claude API failures retry with capped exponential backoff, then fail loudly (ClaudeCallFailed) rather than sending an unverified briefing
